bull.b: Strong sales growth combined with very high gross margins indicates attractive product economics and expanding commercial traction. If maintained, this combination can support reinvestment in sales and development while creating a foundation for improving operating leverage over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Broad product demand and portfolio momentum
bull.b: Growth across multiple ophthalmic products reduces reliance on a single commercial driver and demonstrates demand for Harrow’s broader portfolio. Rising prescriptions, ordering accounts, and surgical adoption can support durable revenue expansion as commercial coverage and field productivity continue to develop.

TYRVAYA materially broadens Harrow’s dry-eye offering alongside VEVYE and adds an established commercial team and distribution presence. The expanded portfolio can improve physician choice, increase productivity across customer calls, and provide a structural source of future revenue growth.

bear.t: Higher leverage and thin equity cushion
bear.b: A more debt-funded balance sheet reduces financial flexibility and makes the company more sensitive to operating setbacks, refinancing needs, and interest obligations. The thin equity cushion also limits room to absorb execution issues or fund additional growth without increasing dilution or leverage.

Weak bottom-line performance shows that strong gross margins have not yet translated into consistent profitability, suggesting substantial operating or non-operating burdens. Continued investment and acquisition-related spending could delay earnings improvement and constrain internally generated capital.

Meeting the annual outlook depends on a substantial second-half acceleration across product growth, channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and integration. Reimbursement pressure in ASC settings adds a structural adoption hurdle, increasing the risk that execution falls short of plan.
